rejected_candidates.candidate: equation (2.7), reduction of structured backward error to a minimum-infinity-norm underdetermined system
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper's reduction is exact vectorization and diagonal scaling. The compiled library contains no underdetermined minimum-infinity-norm theorem; the close source modules are uncompiled. Its remaining formal core is therefore Mathlib-level linear algebra rather than a T1/T2 library advantage, and a full optimization existence treatment would extend beyond the brief paper derivation.

rejected_candidates.candidate: equation (2.8), the square-root(t+n) comparison from the pseudoinverse 2-norm solution
rejected_candidates.reason: Once the 2-norm minimizer is supplied, the displayed comparison is the standard finite-dimensional relation between the 2-norm and infinity norm and is too easy for T3. The pseudoinverse/QR facts are invoked rather than proved in detail.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the symmetric, Toeplitz, and augmented least-squares constructions in Section 4
rejected_candidates.reason: These specialize the general B and Y matrices and discuss costs, scaling, or experiments. They do not supply a separate difficult theorem proof, and the directly relevant structured and least-squares NumStability files are unavailable source-only modules.

rejected_candidates.candidate: condition estimator and numerical examples in Sections 3 and 5
rejected_candidates.reason: The estimator is cited from earlier Hager/Higham work and the tables are experiments, not new universally quantified results proved in this paper.

T1.decision: Skipped. No paper-proved target needs exactly one substantial result from the frozen compiled library. Generic matrix/norm adapters are Mathlib-level, while close underdetermined and perturbation modules are unavailable to L.

T2.decision: Skipped. No source proof needs at least two distinct substantial compiled NumStability results. The paper's structured backward-error and condition arguments are paper-specific exact derivations.

T3.decision: Selected the sharp componentwise-box supremum at the core of equations (3.3)-(3.4). It requires the full upper-bound and attainable-sign proof, is not a Mathlib import, and has no corresponding result in the compiled or source NumStability library that gives L a material advantage.

selection_policy: Use only mathematical conclusions whose statement and derivation are present in this paper.
Treat source-only NumStability modules as unavailable to condition L.
Do not classify generic matrix and norm adapters as substantial library results when Mathlib already supplies their content.
Retain the paper's attainable-sign sharpness claim rather than reducing equation (3.4) to only its easy upper inequality.
Do not turn the numerical experiments or externally cited estimator into formal theorem tasks.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source, its importable compiled subset, and Mathlib.
